forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 21%. No formal AGI claim. June 2026 noise: Anthropic announced Claude Partner Network Services Track / Project Glasswing (3 Jun); Microsoft Build pushed coding agents; Hassabis (Decrypt interview, June 2026) reiterated ~50% by 2030. Amodei still leans 2027. Nothing in last 24h shifts the resolution probability.
forecasts.base_rate: Resolution requires a credible public AGI claim from a major lab OR 3+ leading researchers stating AGI achieved, before 1 Jan 2030 (~3.5 yrs out). Definitional disputes raise the bar; labs historically defer transformational claims until capability is unambiguous.

factors_up.factor: Amodei (Anthropic) maintaining ~2027 AGI timeline; competitive pressure across 6+ frontier-tier labs
Capability gains continuing (Stanford AI Index 2026; HLE jump in past year)
AI-automating-AI feedback loops cited by lab leaders

factors_down.factor: No major lab has issued any formal AGI claim as of June 2026
Definitional ambiguity raises bar for the '3+ senior researchers' clause
Hassabis (DeepMind) restating ~50% by 2030 — not a pre-2030 baseline

key_uncertainties: Whether internal capability translates to public AGI declarations before 2030
Whether IPO pressure on OpenAI/Anthropic incentivises or deters such claims
Pace of AI-automating-AI loops in 2027-2029
update_triggers: Formal AGI claim from a frontier lab
Public statement by 2+ senior researchers at OpenAI/Anthropic/DeepMind that AGI is achieved
Major step-change on AGI-relevant evals (METR, HLE, ARC-AGI v3)

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 24%. Latest 2026 signals reinforce yesterday's net-negative read: BCG ~$3.6B AI revenue (25% of 2025 total); UK Big Four cutting graduate intakes 6-30%; UK AI consultants commanding £70-150k. Entry-level squeeze is real but offset by AI specialist hiring, so industry-wide ≥33% headcount/revenue drop remains unlikely by 2030.
forecasts.base_rate: Resolution requires industry-wide ≥33% decline in revenue OR employment vs 2024 baseline by end-2030, attributed primarily to AI by 2+ credible analyses. Such sector contractions in a 6-yr window are historically rare absent broader recession.

factors_up.factor: Generative AI compressing entry-level analyst work; UK Big Four graduate intakes cut 6-30%
Pressure on hourly/headcount-billing models as AI productivity becomes visible to clients
Possibility of a 2027-2029 recession compounding AI-driven restructuring

factors_down.factor: Big 3 currently growing on AI demand: BCG ~$3.6B AI revenue (~25% of 2025)
Net hiring still positive in AI specialist roles; pricing migrating to value-based
Resolution requires '2+ credible analyses attributing primarily to AI' — high evidentiary bar

key_uncertainties: Whether 2027-2030 sees a structural pricing collapse offsetting AI revenue growth
Definition of 'consultancy' (Big 3 strategy vs. broader management/IT consulting)
Macro backdrop: recession vs. soft landing
update_triggers: Major firm announcing >10% headcount cuts citing AI
Industry revenue contraction reported by Source Global / Kennedy / ALM
Shift from time-and-materials to value-based pricing across Big 3

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 4%. PollCheck 7-poll moving average (5 Jun): Reform 27.3%, Lab 18.4%, Con 18.4%, Grn 14.6%, LD 12.3%. No improvement for Labour vs yesterday. Ipsos June note: Reform 8-pt lead but with doubts about readiness for government — a marginal upside but doesn't pull Labour into first place.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: governing parties with sub-25% poll share ~3 yrs from an election rarely recover to first-place finishes. Historic UK base rate for an incumbent recovering this far from this deep a hole is single digits.

factors_up.factor: Election still ~3 yrs away; FPTP can yield plurality on similar share if right splits
Ipsos: doubts over Reform's readiness for government could erode lead
Possible Conservative-Reform split keeps Labour as plurality on similar share

factors_down.factor: Labour at 18.4% in PollCheck average, well behind Reform (27.3%)
PLMR seat model: ~86 Labour seats — implies catastrophic loss
May 2026 local election results consistent with national polls; no rebound visible

key_uncertainties: Whether Reform consolidates or fractures the right-of-centre vote by 2029
Whether Starmer remains Labour leader through to the GE
Macroeconomic trajectory 2027-2029
update_triggers: Labour returning to >25% in 7-poll average
Reform-Conservative formal pact or split
Change in Labour leadership

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 78%. Hassabis (Decrypt, June 2026) restating ~50% AGI by 2030 still leaves substantial probability mass before 2035. Aggregated forecaster surveys (Metaculus, aimultiple ~9,800 predictions) continue to cluster pre-2035. No material June signal vs yesterday.
forecasts.base_rate: Aggregated forecaster surveys (Metaculus, aimultiple's 9,800-prediction analysis, AI Insider surveys) put median AGI before 2035 at 60-80%. Lab leaders (Amodei, Hassabis, Altman) all project pre-2035 with varying confidence.

factors_up.factor: Multiple frontier labs predicting AGI before 2030 with 8+ yrs of buffer
Compute/algorithm trajectory remains exponential; AI-automating-AI compounding
Resolution standard (lab announcement OR 3+ researchers) is fairly soft over 9 yrs

factors_down.factor: Unknown unknowns / capability plateaus (reasoning, long-horizon agency)
Definitional disputes could persist even with strong capability
Possible regulatory or compute shock 2027-2032

key_uncertainties: Whether scaling continues or hits a wall in 2027-2030
Whether 'AGI' as a term retains social meaning by 2035
Geopolitical disruption to compute supply chains
update_triggers: Major capability plateau on frontier benchmarks for >12 months
Formal AGI claim from a major lab
Compute/regulatory shock disrupting frontier training

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 8%. US ODNI Annual Threat Assessment reaffirmed that Chinese leaders 'do not currently plan to execute an invasion of Taiwan'. PLA continues gray-zone (Liaoning April transit, ~159 aircraft/199 vessels tracked) but no movement toward a >72hr blockade in early June 2026. Status quo deterrence holding.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: PRC has never executed a >72hr blockade or assault on Taiwan proper. Major-power initiated wars in any given ~3.5 yr window have low base rate (~5-10%) absent acute trigger.

factors_up.factor: Continued PLA exercises simulating blockade ops (Justice Mission 2025 series)
Xi's domestic political timeline; 2027 PLA modernisation milestone
Risk of accidental escalation from gray-zone activity

factors_down.factor: US ODNI: PRC leadership not currently planning invasion
Massive economic cost to China; semiconductor dependency cuts both ways
Gray-zone coercion remains PRC's preferred lever — substitutes for kinetic action

key_uncertainties: Whether a Taiwan independence-leaning move triggers escalation
US political posture / Trump administration response to a crisis
PLA confidence in joint-force readiness by 2027-2028
update_triggers: PLA mobilisation beyond exercise patterns
Taiwan referendum or formal independence move
PRC ASBM/anti-access deployments to forward bases

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 5%. Latest ONS print (April 2026): headline CPI 2.8%, with the April moderation driven by an 80bp drop in housing/household services as the new energy price cap took effect (1 April). May 2026 release out 20 May but details still trickling. Path to <2.0% in any single month before Jan 2027 still requires another ~80bp move; services CPI remains sticky.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: UK CPI annual rate has been ≥2.0% every month since mid-2021. A drop from 2.8% to <2.0% in <8 months requires ~80bp of disinflation — historically requires sustained negative output gap or commodity shock.

factors_up.factor: Downward trend in CPI (3.3% → 2.8%) March-April; April energy cap drove housing CPI from 5.3% to 1.4%
Possible additional energy/utility base effects in autumn 2026
Weak demand from cooling labour market

factors_down.factor: Services inflation still well above 2%; wage growth ~5%
BoE central projection has CPI back to 2% only in 2027
Only ~7 monthly prints remaining before Jan 2027 deadline

key_uncertainties: Magnitude of energy base effects Q4 2026
Whether services inflation breaks sharply lower
Sterling and commodity price moves
update_triggers: May 2026 CPI print full release / June print mid-July
Sharp drop in Brent/UK natural gas prices
Services CPI breaking below 3.5%

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Down 5pp to 73%. Polymarket on 'highest-grossing 2026' has slid further to ~46% (from 54.5% last week) as Avengers: Doomsday and Toy Story 5 contracts firmed. The $1.5B WW bar is distinct from the domestic-leader market, but the soft drift in market-implied expectations and the still-uncertain China release motivate a small downward revision. Trailer 1 (1B views in 4 days, first ever) keeps the upside case intact.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: prior MCU Spider-Man films opened to massive WW grosses (No Way Home: $1.92B; Far From Home: $1.13B). With Holland's return and MCU reset narrative, $1.5B WW is achievable but requires either a No Way Home-style breakout or a confirmed China slate.

factors_up.factor: Record-shattering trailer engagement (first trailer ever to hit 1B views, in 4 days)
Tom Holland return + post-Doomsday narrative momentum
Light competition in late summer 2026 window

factors_down.factor: Polymarket-implied domestic-leader probability has slid to ~46%
Global theatrical market still ~15-20% below 2019 levels
China access remains uncertain for major MCU releases

key_uncertainties: China release status and gross
Critical reception and word-of-mouth
Avengers: Doomsday (May 2026) cannibalisation
update_triggers: Opening weekend gross
Confirmed China release
Rotten Tomatoes score at release

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 99%. May/June 2026 reporting: Anthropic ~$45B ARR (gross-of-cloud-reseller basis), OpenAI ~$33B ARR — combined ~$78B already clears the $70B threshold. Anthropic's confidential IPO filing (1 June) at ~$965B valuation underlines revenue trajectory. OpenAI CRO disputes Anthropic's figure by ~$8B; even at low end the combined figure clears.
forecasts.base_rate: Resolution requires 'most recent credible reporting' of Q4 2026 ARR to sum to >$70B. Combined figure is already above threshold mid-2026 with ARR growth >5% per month.

factors_up.factor: Combined ARR already ~$78B per credible reporting (May/June 2026)
Both companies still growing ARR materially month-on-month
Anthropic IPO filing supports continued enterprise momentum

factors_down.factor: OpenAI CRO disputes Anthropic ARR by ~$8B — definitional risk
Possible Q3-Q4 enterprise spending pullback
Reporting methodology disputes (gross-of-reseller) could create ambiguity

key_uncertainties: How aggressively each company reports inference vs subscription ARR
Whether a Q4 2026 macro slowdown hits enterprise AI spend
Resolution sensitivity to which 'credible source' is used
update_triggers: Either company reports flat/declining ARR
Formal Q4 2026 disclosure
Audited financials showing lower-than-claimed run rates

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 35%. OBR March 2026 EFO: 1.1% in 2026, 1.6% in 2027; medium-term productivity growth assumed at 1% with labour supply slowing to 0.5% by 2030 — implying trend GDP near 1.5% but with productivity downside risks. AI productivity tailwind remains the main upside not yet in OBR/IFS baseline. No new June signal.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: UK trend growth averaged ~1.7% across the 2010s post-GFC. Reaching >1.5% across an entire decade requires either no recession or productivity recovery offsetting labour-supply drag.

factors_up.factor: OBR assumes productivity growth picking up to 1% in medium term
AI productivity tailwind not yet in baseline forecasts
Planning, energy and defence-spending reforms could lift trend growth

factors_down.factor: Labour supply growth declining to 0.5% by 2030 (ageing, lower migration)
Debt ~95% of GDP into early 2030s constrains fiscal headroom
Productivity has averaged ~0.5% since 2008 — 1% assumption is a stretch

key_uncertainties: Whether AI delivers measurable productivity gains by mid-2030s
Severity of any 2027-2029 downturn
Migration policy trajectory and labour-force participation
update_triggers: OBR upgrading/downgrading medium-term productivity assumption
IFS or NIESR publishing 2030s decadal scenarios
Material change in net migration assumptions
